links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 11, Organizing Files
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: shutil, deleting, os.walk, zipfile and the backup project.

links.title: shutil — High-level file operations
links.why: Exactly what copy, copytree, move and rmtree do when the destination exists, and the archive helpers.

links.title: zipfile — Work with ZIP archives
links.why: ZipFile modes, compression methods, extract and the warning about untrusted archives.

links.title: os — Miscellaneous operating system interfaces
links.why: os.walk with its topdown and pruning rules, os.unlink and os.rmdir.

links.title: pathlib — Object-oriented filesystem paths
links.why: iterdir, glob, Path.walk (3.12) and Path.copy and Path.move (3.14).

links.title: zlib — Compression compatible with gzip
links.why: What the compression levels 0 to 9 and the default level mean.

links.title: os.path — Common pathname manipulations
links.why: getsize, used by the practice program that looks for large files.

links.title: re — Regular expression operations
links.why: sub and group references, used to swap the month and day in a file name.

links.title: PEP 428 – The pathlib module – object-oriented filesystem paths
Python Tutorial: Zip Files - Creating and Extracting Zip Archives
links.why: A walk through creating, reading and extracting ZIP archives with zipfile, the part 4 of this chapter.

links.title: ZIP (file format), Wikipedia
links.why: The history of the format: Phil Katz, Gary Conway and the public-domain release of 14 February 1989.

links.title: Zlib, Wikipedia
links.why: The library under ZIP_DEFLATED: Jean-loup Gailly, Mark Adler and zlib 0.9 of 1 May 1995.

links.title: ZIP file format specification (APPNOTE.TXT)
links.why: The format zipfile reads and writes, as its owners specify it.

links.title: Susan Kare's Macintosh icons, Smithsonian Magazine
links.why: How the trash can and the other first Macintosh icons were drawn in 1983.

links.title: Multics history, multicians.org
links.why: The 1965 paper of Daley and Neumann on the tree-structured file system that os.walk still visits.

links.title: Send2Trash on the Python Package Index
links.why: The third-party module that moves a file into the recycle bin instead of deleting it.
